claim: For MySQL and unspecified dialects the guard refuses double dashes lacking the required separator, nested block-comment openers, and backslash-escaped closing quotes; ordinary backslashes, quoted comment markers and standard comments remain accepted; and CR normalization applies only to comment text, never to literals or identifiers.
source_excerpt: For MySQL (and unspecified dialects), the guard refuses double dashes without the ASCII whitespace/control character required for a MySQL line comment, nested block-comment openers, and backslash-escaped closing quotes. Use spaced arithmetic and doubled quotes instead. This keeps inspection independent of `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` and `ANSI_QUOTES` quote-boundary changes. Ordinary backslashes, quoted comment markers, and standard comments remain accepted; carriage returns inside line comments are normalized only for parser inspection because MySQL ends those comments at LF. The original SQL still reaches the connector after validation.
